hero.h1: Ejector Pump Repair and Replacement in Hinsdale, IL
hero.sub: An alarm going off, a basement toilet that won't drain or a sewer smell near the basin. We repair and replace ejector pumps for basement bathrooms, bars and laundry rooms. Our office is on Spinning Wheel Road. Open 24/7.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber working on the pump and wiring inside a basement pit

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Fixtures below the sewer line can't drain by gravity. A basement toilet, shower, bar sink or laundry drains into a sealed basin, and the ejector pump lifts the wastewater up into the main line. A float switch turns the pump on, and a check valve keeps the water from falling back. If one part fails, the basin fills and backs up into the room.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber working on the discharge pipe of a basement sump pump

blocks.h2: Signs Your Ejector Pump Is Failing

tiles.body: The basin is filling faster than the pump empties it.
The pump is weak or the line is partly blocked.
A worn lid seal or a vent problem.
A stuck float or a failed check valve.

blocks.intro: Finished basements with full baths, bars and laundry rooms are common in Hinsdale, and they all depend on the ejector pump.

items.body: Basements finished in the last 20 years often have pumps nearing the end of their life.
Grease and lint are hard on pumps. A lint trap on the washer hose helps.
A working alarm is the only warning before water reaches the floor. We test it every visit.
In some homes, the ejector basin is the heart of an [overhead sewer system](/hinsdale/overhead-sewer-systems).
Some basins sit in closets or under removable panels. We work carefully around the finishes.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pump Questions From Hinsdale Homeowners

items.q: Can we use the basement bathroom while the alarm is on?
items.preview: No. Stop using every basement drain.
items.answer: No. Stop using every drain that feeds the basin until the pump is fixed, or it will overflow.

items.q: How long does an ejector pump last?
items.answer: Often around 7 to 10 years, depending on use and what goes down the drains.

items.q: Why does our basement smell like sewage?
items.preview: Usually the basin seal, the vent or a dry trap.
items.answer: Usually a worn lid seal, a loose vent connection or a floor drain trap that dried out. We check all three.

items.q: Can you add an ejector pump for a new basement bathroom?
items.answer: Yes. We install the basin, a pump sized for the fixtures and the venting it needs.

items.q: How much does ejector pump replacement cost in Hinsdale?
items.preview: It depends on the pump and basin. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, the basin condition and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
